summary: Prior-art research + independent architecture designs for a multi-user coding-agent collaboration layer

projects.name: Overlap (overlap.dev / overlapcode/overlap)
projects.what: JSONL tracer + self-hosted (Cloudflare) dashboard that gives a TEAM's coding agents real-time file awareness. Parses Claude Code's local session logs passively, detects when two agents/devs target the same file/function/line, and BLOCKS the second agent before it edits ('merge conflicts die before code leaves your machine'). LLM-powered session summaries, org-wide live activity feed.
projects.overlap: Highest overlap with our 'overlap warnings' + presence MVP functions, and explicitly cross-developer ('your agent talks to your teammates' agents'). Stops short at file/function/line-level collision: no diagnosis model, no hypotheses/evidence, no semantic matching of differently-worded tasks, no decision history. Injection into the agent is limited to block/warn messages, not relevant findings.
projects.learn: The passive ingestion trick: read the JSONL session logs Claude Code already writes to disk — zero agent compliance, no plugins, no token overhead. Also the self-hosted-on-free-tier deployment story and 'GitHub sees the past, we see the present' positioning — copy that framing.
projects.activity: 1 star, created 2026-01, last push 2026-03 (stalled); hosted overlap.dev landing is live

projects.name: Drift (driftlabs.io / SHC-Labs)
projects.what: SaaS 'real-time coordination for humans and AI agents in the same codebase' — server-enforced intent declarations before file edits, conflict checks across every dev and agent, a persistent 'team brain' memory with a 3D visualizer, MCP tools (declare intent, check conflicts, query knowledge, broadcast changes). Intents become draft PRs, conflicts open GitHub issues.
projects.overlap: Closest concept match among products: intent sharing + cross-user conflict detection + shared team memory in one system, explicitly marketed at 'ten devs and forty agents'. But it is closed-source SaaS (only a 0-star CLI on GitHub), conflicts appear file/intent-level not diagnosis-level, and memory is generic facts/decisions — no hypothesis lifecycle, no extending someone else's root-cause chain.
projects.learn: Its GitHub-native surfacing (intents→draft PRs, conflicts→issues, scores→PR reviews) is a smart adoption path: 'makes GitHub better, not a replacement'. Validates the exact problem narrative ('every engineer had their own agent editing the same files overnight'). Being closed-source, it leaves the open-source slot empty.
projects.activity: Closed source; drift-cli repo 0 stars, pushed 2026-05; product site live

projects.name: asynkor
projects.what: Go MCP server: 'file leasing for AI agent teams'. Agents declare work + acquire file leases (asynkor_start), get a team briefing (active work, leases, parked sessions, memory, inbox), detect overlap via path-level + plan-text similarity, save compounding team memory (asynkor_remember), park/resume work across agents, and open async question threads (ask/inbox/reply) — plus a live dashboard.
projects.overlap: Feature-union closest to our 5-function MVP: presence, intent, overlap detection (including semantic-ish plan-text similarity), team memory, agent-to-agent questions, and handoff. Stops short: memory is unstructured notes not a diagnosis graph; no hypothesis status/evidence/rejected-approaches; injection is pull-based (agent must call asynkor_briefing), not proactive; no human approval gates; tiny and apparently stalled.
projects.learn: Steal the MCP tool-surface design almost wholesale (briefing / start-with-lease / check / park / inspect / ask / inbox / reply) — it is a clean vocabulary for agent coordination. Also 'park' as a first-class handoff primitive and plan-text similarity as a cheap semantic overlap heuristic.
projects.activity: 50 stars, created 2026-04, last push 2026-05-03 (looks stalled); hosted asynkor.com dashboard

projects.name: mcp_agent_mail (Dicklesworthstone)
projects.what: 'Gmail for your coding agents' — HTTP FastMCP server giving agents memorable identities, inbox/outbox with GFM messages, searchable threads, an agent directory, and advisory file-reservation leases with an optional pre-commit guard. Backed by Git (human-auditable artifacts) + SQLite (indexing). Integrates the beads issue tracker.
projects.overlap: The best-known open agent-to-agent async coordination layer, and multi-machine capable (HTTP server over 'one or more codebases'). But its framing and use cases are one developer's parallel agents, not many developers; knowledge is free-form mail, not structured diagnoses; overlap detection is file leases + FTS search, not semantic; nothing is proactively injected — agents must check their inbox.
projects.learn: Advisory (not mandatory) file leases + pre-commit guard as the enforcement spectrum; git-backed human-auditable message artifacts; memorable adjective+noun agent identities; resource:// URIs for cheap inbox reads. Its README is also a masterclass in explaining the coordination problem.

projects.name: omem / ourmem
projects.what: Rust self-hostable 'shared memory that never forgets': Personal/Team/Organization memory Spaces with provenance-tracked cross-user sharing, quality-gated auto-share rules, 7-decision reconciliation (CREATE/MERGE/SUPERSEDE/CONTRADICT/...), 11-stage hybrid retrieval, and Claude Code/OpenCode/OpenClaw/MCP plugins with SessionStart auto-recall, mid-session KeywordRecall, and SessionEnd auto-capture hooks.
projects.overlap: The most complete open-source cross-user memory system, and it DOES do proactive injection (session-start recall + keyword-triggered recall of team memories). Stops short: memories are generic facts/decisions/preferences — no work-in-flight presence, no live intent, no conflict/overlap detection, no diagnosis tree with hypothesis statuses that another agent can extend.
projects.learn: Its reconciliation vocabulary (SUPERSEDE / SUPPORT / CONTRADICT / CONTEXTUALIZE) is 80% of the semantics we need for a living diagnosis graph — reuse it. Also: quality-gated auto-share rules, provenance + staleness detection on shared copies, and the hook set (SessionStart/KeywordRecall/SessionEnd/Compaction) as the injection mechanism for Claude Code.
projects.activity: 201 stars, created 2026-03, last push 2026-05; hosted ourmem.ai

projects.name: ByteRover CLI / Cipher (campfirein)
projects.what: Formerly Cipher; 'portable memory layer for autonomous coding agents' and a hosted platform positioned as the central memory for an entire dev team. Git-like workflow for context: curate project memory locally, brv push to a shared team workspace, teammates brv pull. System 1 (concepts/business logic) + System 2 (model reasoning steps) + Workspace (team-shared) memory; MCP across Cursor/Claude Code/Windsurf etc.
projects.overlap: Real cross-user, cross-agent team memory with explicit push/pull sharing, and it even stores reasoning traces (System 2). Stops short: knowledge is curated project context, not live in-flight work; no presence, no overlap/conflict detection, no diagnosis structure, and injection is query/pull-based rather than proactive; team features increasingly gravitate to the hosted SaaS.
projects.learn: The git-metaphor UX (push/pull context) lowers adoption friction for developers; the System 1 / System 2 split (facts vs reasoning) is a useful schema idea — our diagnosis chains are essentially structured System 2 memory.

projects.name: Entire CLI (entireio, ex-GitHub-CEO Thomas Dohmke)
projects.what: Open-source (Go) CLI that hooks into the git workflow to capture every AI agent session — prompts, transcripts, reasoning — as 'checkpoints' indexed alongside commits, stored on a separate git branch so main history stays clean. Companion 'skills' repo lets agents search past work, explain code from session history, and hand off sessions; supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, more via external-agents. $60M seed, entire.io platform on top.
projects.overlap: The strongest-funded bet on cross-developer agent context — and because storage is git, context genuinely travels across the team. But it is fundamentally retrospective: context is keyed to commits/pushes, exactly the 'too late' point our concept attacks. No presence, no in-flight intent, no overlap detection, no hypothesis model; injection is on-demand (agent invokes a search/explain skill), not proactive.
projects.learn: The separate-git-branch storage pattern for agent metadata (no server needed, works with existing remotes, zero history pollution) — consider it as an optional transport for our diagnosis records. Also their session-handoff skill as prior art for structured handoffs.

projects.name: beads (Steve Yegge)
projects.what: 'A memory upgrade for your coding agent' — git-native graph issue tracker designed for agents: issues, dependencies, discovered work, all stored in the repo and synced via normal git push/pull, with JSON 'robot flags' (bv --robot-plan, --robot-insights: PageRank, critical path, parallel tracks) for agent consumption. Used by Gas Town as its work substrate.
projects.overlap: Proves the git-based cross-developer agent-coordination pattern at scale (25k stars): every dev's agent reads/writes the same issue graph. Stops short: granularity is issues/tasks/dependencies — not observation→hypothesis→evidence chains; sync is at git speed (not live presence); no semantic overlap detection between in-flight sessions; no proactive injection into other agents' contexts.
projects.learn: The distribution model: knowledge lives in the repo, syncs with tooling devs already trust, works offline — a serious alternative to our central-service architecture worth offering as a backend. Also the --robot-* deterministic JSON interface convention for agent-facing CLIs.

projects.name: ai-team-sync (pvestal)
projects.what: Coordinates multiple AI coding agents of DIFFERENT devs on one repo: declared sessions ('ats session start -s src/auth/** -d "Refactoring auth to JWT"'), advisory/exclusive file scope locks, and a persistent decision log (choice, alternatives considered, reason) that outlives the chat session. Surfaces in VS Code toasts, browser dashboard, CLI, and MCP; agent identity via ATS_AGENT.
projects.overlap: Explicitly targets our exact scenario ('when two devs both tell their AI agents to change the same files, nobody knows until conflicting PRs appear') and its decision log covers our 'technical decisions' knowledge type including alternatives+rationale. Stops short: glob-level locks only, no semantic matching, no diagnosis model, no proactive context injection, zero traction.
projects.learn: Its decision-record schema (choice / considered / reason) and the advisory-vs-exclusive lock modes; also the VS Code toast surface — human-visible notifications matter as much as agent-visible ones.

projects.name: tempo-agents (kgarg2468)
projects.what: Hackathon-grade 'real-time conflict prediction for AI-coding teams': extracts intent fingerprints from live dirty-worktree diffs, predicts SEMANTIC collisions (contract changes, architectural ownership conflicts, incompatible API shapes, intent-level overlap), classifies them via a three-level interruption ladder (clear / notice / stop), and routes blocking conflicts through a human-approved decision that issues owner/adapter work orders to the affected agents.
projects.overlap: Conceptually the closest thing to our semantic + architectural conflict detector — it explicitly names the gap ('git only speaks when work is ready to merge; Tempo catches semantic contract changes and intent-level overlap earlier'). Stops short: prototype for a challenge, 1 star, dead after 2 days of commits; no diagnosis sharing, no team memory, conflict-only.
projects.learn: The design ideas: intent fingerprints computed locally from live diffs (privacy-preserving — only compact fingerprints leave the machine), the escalation ladder instead of binary blocking, and human-approved resolution episodes with complementary work orders. This is a blueprint for our conflict-detector component.

projects.name: Lore (Tanagram) + Claude Code native session sharing + Amp Workspaces
projects.what: The 'share the transcript' category: Lore renders full Claude Code/Codex/Cowork sessions as shareable links (private/workspace/public) and lets a teammate FORK a thread into a fresh session with a distilled handoff. Claude Code itself now has native session-share links. Sourcegraph's Amp publishes threads (full reasoning trace, tool calls, edits) to team workspaces by default.
projects.overlap: Covers cross-user visibility of what an agent did and even handoff-with-context (Lore fork). Stops short everywhere else: passive, human-initiated, transcript-granularity (no structured hypotheses/evidence to query or extend), no presence, no matching, no conflict detection, no automatic injection; Lore and Amp are closed SaaS.
projects.learn: Lore's 'fork with distilled handoff tailored to what you want to do next' is the best existing UX for continuing a colleague's session — our diagnosis records should support the same 'continue from here' affordance. Amp's default-share-to-workspace shows teams accept ambient sharing of agent work.
projects.activity: Lore: active SaaS; Amp: 40k+ teams claimed in 2026; Claude Code session sharing: shipped natively

projects.name: CCPM (automazeio/ccpm)
projects.what: Project-management skill system for Claude Code: PRD → epic → task decomposition, GitHub Issues as the coordination database, git worktrees for parallel agent execution, progress posted as issue comments so humans and other agents can follow along.
projects.overlap: Mostly single-dev multi-agent orchestration, but its use of GitHub Issues as the shared bus makes progress visible across the team and is genuinely cross-user at the task/progress level. No diagnosis knowledge, no semantic matching, no injection, coordination granularity is the issue thread.
projects.learn: 'Use infrastructure the team already has (GitHub Issues) as the audit trail' — lowers trust barrier. Its strict traceability discipline (every code change traces to spec) is a good norm for our decision records.

projects.name: claude-flow/ruflo (ruvnet), claude-swarm (parruda/swarm), vibe-kanban, Conductor, Gas Town, agent-teams (777genius), Claude Code Agent Teams
projects.what: The single-user multi-agent orchestrator cluster: claude-flow/ruflo (65k stars, swarm meta-harness with its own shared memory/hive-mind for ITS agents), claude-swarm→parruda/swarm (tree of Claude sessions via MCP, used inside Shopify), vibe-kanban (27k, kanban for your coding agents), Conductor (closed Mac app, parallel Claude Code in worktrees), Gas Town (17k, Yegge's multi-agent workspace manager on beads), Anthropic's experimental Agent Teams (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS).
projects.overlap: Noted per the task's critical distinction: all coordinate ONE developer's many agents on one machine/workspace. Their 'shared memory' and messaging are intra-swarm. None share knowledge across different developers' machines, none model diagnoses, none inject into another human's agent session.
projects.learn: claude-flow's memory/hive-mind shows agents will actually use a shared blackboard when tools make it trivial; Gas Town/beads shows convoy/work-item patterns; Agent Teams' teammate-mailbox UX in Claude Code is the native surface our connector should eventually feel like. These are also our future integration targets, not competitors.
projects.activity: ruflo 65,748 stars (active); vibe-kanban 27,496; gastown 17,191 (active); all very much alive

projects.name: Letta (MemGPT), Zep, Cognee, Mem0/OpenMemory
projects.what: General agent-memory infrastructure: Letta (23.9k, stateful agents with self-editing memory), Zep (4.8k, temporal knowledge-graph memory), Cognee (29.2k, memory pipelines into graph+vector), Mem0 (61.6k, universal memory layer with a four-scope model: user_id / agent_id / run_id / org_id for shared organizational context).
projects.overlap: These provide multi-tenant, org-scoped memory primitives — the storage substrate for a team brain — and Mem0's org_id scope plus Zep's temporal graph are directly reusable. None are coding-agent coordination systems: no notion of repo/branch/in-flight work, no conflict detection, no proactive injection into coding sessions, no diagnosis semantics.
projects.learn: Build ON one of these rather than reinventing storage: Mem0's scope-composition-at-retrieval pattern and Zep's temporal invalidation (facts that become false — exactly like rejected hypotheses) map cleanly onto a diagnosis graph. Cognee for the graph+embedding hybrid.

projects.name: Long tail of team-memory MCP servers (knowledgeplane, Loom, NexMem, itdove/lore, chroma-memory-mcp, smg-claude-memory-mcp, BrainFlow, evalops/shared-memory-mcp)
projects.what: A dozen small (0–31 star) MCP servers offering 'shared team memory' for coding agents: knowledge-graph + vector search + auto-consolidation (knowledgeplane), team knowledge for Claude Code/Cursor (Loom), pluggable DB backends (NexMem), git-shared vector memory (smg), cross-team knowledge (itdove/lore, created 2026-07-23!), and shared context within one agentic run (evalops).
projects.overlap: Confirms strong demand for the memory half of the concept, and that a bare 'team memory MCP' is commoditized. All are store/search primitives: no presence, no in-flight work model, no overlap detection, no hypothesis lifecycle, injection at best a session-start dump. None has traction.
projects.learn: The lesson is strategic: do NOT ship 'yet another team memory MCP' as the headline — that lane is crowded and undifferentiated. Differentiation must come from the diagnosis graph + conflict detection + proactive injection. evalops' 'coordination tax / token efficiency' framing is useful messaging.
projects.activity: 0–31 stars each; several created within the last 4 months; mostly single-author

projects.name: Parachute (+ Liveblocks/Yjs plugin) — CRDT approaches
projects.what: Parachute: multi-user cloud IDE where each dev brings their own agent; Yjs CRDTs sync files/cursors/orchestrator state, and a master Orchestrator AI detects same-file collisions, manages locks, and reassigns late agents. Liveblocks ships a plugin adding Yjs/realtime skills for AI coding assistants (for building collaborative apps, not for coordinating agents).
projects.overlap: Parachute solves cross-user agent conflict — but by forcing everyone into one shared cloud workspace, abandoning the local-first reality our concept targets (devs on their own machines/branches). CRDTs for agent coordination exist only as demos. No diagnosis knowledge, no semantic layer.
projects.learn: If we need real-time co-presence state (who is where, live diagnosis-tree edits), Yjs/Automerge over WebSocket is proven and cheap; Parachute's Y.Map orchestrator state + observed event array is a workable pattern for our presence store. But the shared-IDE model is the anti-pattern to avoid.
projects.activity: Parachute 0 stars (Mar 2026, dormant); Liveblocks company active

projects.name: .track (ekaya97) + agent-board (wilsonwu) + Agent Cockpit
projects.what: Passive observability layer projects: .track observes agents purely via Claude Code hooks (auto-register with NATO alias, per-file conflict warnings, session summaries, git-shared markdown tickets 'shared across worktrees and collaborators'); agent-board is a Socket.IO dashboard of team developer + agent activity fed by a VS Code extension; Agent Cockpit is a local control room for one dev's parallel sessions.
projects.overlap: These are awareness dashboards. .track's hook-based passive capture and git-shared tickets edge toward cross-user, agent-board is explicitly team-wide telemetry. All stop at 'see what is happening': no knowledge model, no semantic matching, no injection, no diagnosis.
projects.learn: .track's hook matrix (SessionStart→register, Edit→track+conflict-check, Bash→detect test runs, SessionEnd→summary) is exactly the event set our local agent-connector should capture from Claude Code — copy it. Zero-token passive observation is the right default.

projects.name: Continue.dev team features + Sourcegraph enterprise context
projects.what: Continue Hub lets orgs share assistants/rules/MCP blocks and mines 'dev data' from AI-assisted sessions org-wide; Sourcegraph provides shared code-graph/search context to agents (and Amp, covered above) at enterprise scale.
projects.overlap: Both share CONFIGURATION and CODEBASE context across a team, not in-flight investigation knowledge. No presence, no diagnosis, no conflict detection. Closed/hosted for the team parts.
projects.learn: Continue's org-level 'blocks' registry is a good model for distributing our connector config/policies across a team; Sourcegraph shows the value of a precise code-symbol graph — our symbol-level overlap detector could piggyback on tree-sitter/SCIP indexing rather than building its own.

priorArt.gapAnalysis: Does anything already do cross-user diagnosis sharing + proactive injection for coding agents? No — nothing combines them, and most systems have neither. The landscape decomposes into five clusters, each covering a different fragment: (1) FILE-COLLISION COORDINATORS (Overlap, asynkor, ai-team-sync, Drift, mcp_agent_mail, Parachute): real cross-user, real-time, pre-commit — but their unit of knowledge is a file path/glob/lease or at best a plan-text similarity score. They can say 'Bob's agent is editing auth.ts', never 'Bob's agent already rejected the caching hypothesis for this bug, with evidence'. tempo-agents sketched semantic/architectural conflict classes (contract changes, ownership conflicts, intent overlap) but died as a 1-star hackathon prototype. (2) TEAM MEMORY LAYERS (omem, ByteRover/Cipher, Mem0 org-scope, Letta/Zep/Cognee, plus a dozen 0-30-star team-memory MCPs): cross-user, persistent, semantically searchable, and omem even has proactive session-start/keyword injection hooks — but they store unstructured facts/preferences/decisions with no model of in-flight work (repo/branch/status), no hypothesis lifecycle (proposed/partially_confirmed/rejected), no evidence chains another agent can extend, and no overlap/conflict detection. (3) SESSION SHARERS (Entire, Lore, Amp workspaces, Claude Code native share): cross-user but retrospective and transcript-granular — you can read or fork what a colleague's agent did, but nothing matches your current task against their in-flight investigation or pushes their findings into your session. (4) GIT-SYNCED WORK GRAPHS (beads, Backlog.md, CCPM-on-GitHub-Issues): cross-user shared state via git/GitHub, but at issue/task granularity, at git sync latency, with no semantic layer. (5) SINGLE-USER ORCHESTRATORS (claude-flow/ruflo, claude-swarm, vibe-kanban, Conductor, Gas Town, Agent Teams): huge stars, but coordinate one developer's agents; their 'shared memory' never crosses machines/users. THE OPEN GAP — our wedge — is the intersection no one occupies: (a) a STRUCTURED LIVING DIAGNOSIS GRAPH (observation → hypotheses with status → evidence → root-cause chain → rejected approaches → open questions) that agents of DIFFERENT developers can extend and contradict rather than overwrite — the closest existing semantics are omem's reconcile verbs (SUPERSEDE/SUPPORT/CONTRADICT) and Zep's temporal fact invalidation, but neither is applied to debugging knowledge; (b) SEMANTIC MATCHING OF IN-FLIGHT TASKS across different vocabulary ('login 500s' ≈ 'JWT validation regression'), which nobody does — collision tools match paths, memory tools match queries the agent explicitly makes; (c) PROACTIVE INJECTION of another developer's relevant findings into a live session (hook-driven push, not inbox-checking or manual search) — only omem does push-injection at all, and only of generic memories; (d) DIAGNOSTIC/ARCHITECTURAL CONFLICT DETECTION — 'two devs hold contradictory root-cause theories for the same symptom' or 'these two in-flight fixes embody incompatible designs' — exists nowhere, not even as a prototype beyond tempo's abandoned sketch; (e) HUMAN APPROVAL GATES for sensitive payloads (full diffs) — only mcp_agent_mail's advisory-lease/pre-commit-guard philosophy gestures at consent. Market signal: every true cross-user coordination attempt is <100 stars and most stalled within 2 months (Overlap, asynkor, tempo, Parachute, ai-team-sync) — the demand is validated by their repeated independent invention and by Drift/Entire raising money on adjacent theses, but no open-source project has credibly landed it; the >4k-star projects are all in the other clusters. Recommended borrowings: Overlap/.track's passive JSONL+hooks capture (zero agent compliance), asynkor's MCP tool vocabulary, omem's reconciliation verbs + injection hooks, mcp_agent_mail's advisory leases + git-auditable artifacts, tempo's escalation ladder + local intent fingerprints for privacy, beads/Entire's git-as-transport option for teams that refuse a central server, and Mem0/Zep as the storage substrate instead of hand-rolled pgvector.

# Protocols & Landscape Research — Alignment Recommendations

## 1. Agent interop protocols

**Google A2A (Linux Foundation)** — v1.0.1 (May 2026), 150+ supporting orgs, integrated into Google/Microsoft/AWS platforms; production use in supply chain, finserv, insurance. Design center: *opaque service-to-service task delegation* — Agent Cards for discovery, task/artifact lifecycle, request/response between long-running agent endpoints. It is NOT a shared-state or knowledge-graph protocol, and it assumes agents are network-addressable services, not ephemeral CLI sessions on laptops behind NAT. **Verdict: ignore for MVP.** Our topology is hub-and-spoke (every agent talks to the team service, agents never dial each other directly), which needs an API + MCP, not A2A. Revisit only if "agent-to-agent questions" later becomes direct peer messaging — A2A 1.x's extension mechanism (custom data/RPC methods/state machines) would be the standards-track home for that, so keep question/answer payloads as self-contained JSON that could be wrapped in an A2A extension without redesign.

**IBM ACP (BeeAI)** — merged into A2A under LF AI & Data in Aug 2025; A2A absorbed its stateful/async concepts; repos are historical. **Verdict: dead — ignore entirely; never target it.**

**AGNTCY (Cisco → Linux Foundation, July 2025)** — discovery (OASF schema), identity, messaging (SLIM), observability for enterprise "Internet of Agents." 65+ companies, but it is heavyweight service-mesh-for-agents infrastructure, again service-to-service. **Verdict: ignore.** At most, crib OASF's idea of structured agent capability metadata for our presence records.

**Zed's Agent Client Protocol (ACP — the *other* ACP, Aug 2025)** — editor↔agent JSON-RPC over stdio; adopted by JetBrains (whole IDE suite), Zed natively; registry lists Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Copilot, Goose, 25+ agents; Devin Desktop shipped it June 2026. **Verdict: this is the sleeper hit for us.** ACP sessions stream exactly what we want to observe (prompts, plans, tool calls, edits) in a normalized format across agents. Recommended path: Claude Code hooks first (fastest, richest), then an **ACP proxy connector** (sits between editor and agent, mirrors session events to the team service) as the agent-agnostic observation layer — one connector covers every ACP agent instead of N hook systems.

## 2. MCP as delivery mechanism

Spec trajectory: 2025-06-18 (elicitation, structured tool output) → 2025-11-25 (tasks) → **2026-07-28 (RC out, GA July 28): stateless protocol**, handshake removed, extensions framework, and — critical for us — server-initiated requests (sampling/elicitation) only allowed *while processing a client request*; stateless mode drops unsolicited server→client notifications and resource subscriptions; SEP-2322 replaces server-initiated calls with multi-round-trip `InputRequiredResult`.

**Implication: an MCP server cannot push unsolicited context into a live session.** Notifications/`resources/updated` are client-mediated and Claude Code/Cursor do not inject them into model context. MCP is a **pull** channel.

**Verdict: yes, build the MCP server — it's the only transport all three targets (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI) support — but split responsibilities:**
- *Pull (MCP tools)*: `search_related_work`, `get_team_context`, `register_session`, `publish_diagnosis`, `extend_diagnosis`, `ask_agent`. Use MCP resources for diagnosis-tree documents; use elicitation for the human approval gate (share-full-diff consent). Target 2026-07-28 stateless from day one (12-month legacy deprecation window is already running).
- *Push (per-agent thin adapters)*: Claude Code hooks — `SessionStart`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`PostToolUse` `additionalContext` is the only reliable unsolicited-injection path; Cursor via generated rules files; lowest common denominator = writing an `AGENTS.md`-style context file the agent reads. Proactive hints ride the hook adapter, never MCP.

## 3. Commercial team-context landscape

| Tool | Team sharing today | Missing |
|---|---|---|
| Cursor | Team rules; Memories (project-level persistent facts, per-user) | No cross-user memory; org-wide KB only "planned" |
| Copilot | Spaces: curated docs/code/policy hubs; memory emerging | Static curation; nothing live |
| Windsurf/Devin Desktop (Cognition, merged Dec 2025→June 2026) | Devin Knowledge (curated org KB), Memories (~48h learned), codemaps, shared Spaces w/ git worktrees + shared agent context | Closest competitor; still curated-knowledge + own-agents-only, not cross-developer in-flight diagnosis |
| Sourcegraph | Org-wide code intelligence/search as context | Code-state, not work-state |

**Every product shares *curated or learned* knowledge; none shares *live in-flight* work state (who is debugging what right now, competing hypotheses, rejected approaches).** Demand exists — see anthropics/claude-code issue #38536 "Shared Team Memory." The diagnosis graph + presence + overlap detection is genuine white space; ship it before Cognition extends Spaces cross-user.

## 4. OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions

Status: still **Development** (not stable); moved to a dedicated GenAI conventions repo at v1.42.0 (June 2026) for faster cadence; covers LLM spans, agent spans, prompt/completion events, metrics; attribute churn expected, `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` available. **Verdict: align the observation layer only.** Name raw session-observation events with `gen_ai.*` attributes and pin the semconv version — this makes the connector's event stream exportable to any OTel backend for free and future-proofs against agent-observability tooling. Do NOT model the diagnosis graph on OTel — it's telemetry, not knowledge; your hypothesis/evidence/root-cause schema is the differentiator and has no existing standard.

## 5. Summary

- **Build on**: MCP (pull tools + resources + elicitation approval gates; target 2026-07-28 stateless), Claude Code hooks (push/injection), Zed ACP proxy (agent-agnostic observation, phase 2).
- **Stay compatible with**: OTel GenAI attributes for observation events (pinned version); A2A extension-shaped payloads for future peer messaging; `AGENTS.md`-file injection as universal fallback.
- **Ignore**: A2A core (wrong topology), IBM ACP (dead/merged), AGNTCY (enterprise service mesh, wrong layer), waiting for OTel stability (no timeline).
- **Differentiate on**: live in-flight diagnosis graph + cross-user overlap detection — verified absent from Cursor, Copilot Spaces, Devin Desktop, Sourcegraph.

# Claude Code Integration Surface — Ground Truth (verified locally + against code.claude.com/docs, 2026-07-24)

## 1. Hooks

Common stdin JSON for every event: `session_id`, `prompt_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`, `effort`, `hook_event_name`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`. Command hooks get this on stdin; HTTP hooks exist too (POST body) — a hook can call our team service directly with no local script. Hooks can be defined in `~/.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json` (committable — team distribution vector), `.claude/settings.local.json`, plugins (`hooks/hooks.json`), and skill/agent frontmatter. `"async": true` runs a command hook non-blocking; its output is delivered to Claude on the next turn. Prompt-based and agent-based hooks (LLM evaluates a condition) also exist.

The event list is much larger than the classic ten. Relevant ones:

| Event | Extra input | Can block (exit 2 / decision) | Can inject `additionalContext` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | `source` (startup/resume/fork), `model`, `agent_type`, `session_title` | No | Yes (start of conversation; re-runs on resume) |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `prompt` | Yes — `decision:"block"` erases prompt | Yes (plain stdout OR `additionalContext`; alongside prompt) |
| `PreToolUse` | `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id` | Yes — `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision`: `allow`/`deny`/`ask`/`defer`, plus `updatedInput` to rewrite tool args | Yes (next to tool result). `deny` reason is shown to Claude |
| `PermissionRequest` | like PreToolUse + `permission_suggestions` | Yes — `decision.behavior` allow/deny, `updatedInput` | No (decision-only) |
| `PostToolUse` | `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response`, `duration_ms` | No (already ran; exit 2 stderr shown to Claude) | Yes |
| `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch` | tool error / batch info | Batch: yes | Yes |
| `Notification` | `message`, `title`, `notification_type` | No | No |
| `Stop` / `SubagentStop` | `stop_hook_active`, `last_assistant_message`, `background_tasks`; SubagentStop adds `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `agent_transcript_path` | Yes — `decision:"block"` forces continuation (auto-override after 8 blocks) | Yes (end of turn) |
| `SubagentStart` | — | No | Yes |
| `PreCompact` / `PostCompact` | `trigger`, `custom_instructions` | Pre: yes | No |
| `SessionEnd` | `reason` | No | No (session over) |
| `FileChanged` | `file_path`, `event` — fires on external file edits | No | No |
| `TeammateIdle`, `TaskCreated/Completed`, `ConfigChange`, `WorktreeCreate/Remove`, `Setup`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `MessageDisplay`, `Elicitation` | (agent-teams / tasks / infra) | varies | mostly no |

`additionalContext` (in `hookSpecificOutput`) is wrapped in a system-reminder, invisible in the UI; >10k chars is spilled to a file with a preview. Docs warn: phrase it as factual statements, not imperative commands, or prompt-injection defenses trigger. Injection-capable events: SessionStart, Setup, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit(+Expansion), PreToolUse, PostToolUse(+Failure/Batch), Stop, SubagentStop.

## 2. Transcripts on disk

`~/.claude/projects/<path-slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl`, append-only JSONL (verified: 30–55 MB files, live-updated). Record envelope: `type` (`user`, `assistant`, `attachment`, `system`, `summary`, `queue-operation`, `file-history-snapshot`, `ai-title`, `last-prompt`) plus `uuid`, `parentUuid` (tree structure), `sessionId`, `timestamp`, `cwd`, `gitBranch`, `version`, `isSidechain`, `promptId`. `assistant` records carry full API `message` (content blocks: `text`/`thinking`/`tool_use`, `model`, `usage`); `user` records carry prompts and `tool_result`s (`toolUseResult`). Subagent transcripts: `<slug>/<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` (verified), plus `tool-results/` and `workflows/` dirs. A daemon can trivially `tail -F`/fsevents-watch these and reconstruct everything the agent saw and did — including `cwd` + `gitBranch` per record, which is exactly our work-context envelope. Caveat: contains raw private content; any uploader must summarize/redact locally first.

## 3. MCP

Registration: `claude mcp add` with scopes `local` (default), `project` (`.mcp.json` at repo root, checked in — our team-distribution vector), `user`; or JSON in `~/.claude.json`. Transports: stdio, HTTP (`streamable-http` alias), SSE, WebSocket; env-var expansion in `.mcp.json`; OAuth supported. Tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`; PreToolUse matchers can target them. Resources are @-mention pull only. Critically: **push now exists** — an MCP server declaring the `claude/channel` capability can push messages into a live session (channels, research preview, opt-in `--channels` flag; Team/Enterprise orgs must enable). So team updates can be pushed, not just pulled — but it's preview-gated; hooks remain the stable injection path. Tool-search auto-defers large tool sets (our server should keep few, well-described tools).

## 4. Shaping the agent to call our tools

Reliability order, per docs + observed behavior in this very session (the installed context-mode plugin successfully forced tool usage via hooks): (1) **hook-injected system reminders** — deterministic delivery, and PreToolUse `deny` with a reason redirects Claude to our tool ("use `search_related_work` first") — strongest; (2) **skills** — good for named workflows, but trigger-dependent; (3) **CLAUDE.md** — always loaded but advisory, degrades under long context. Best pattern: MCP tools + a thin hook layer that reminds/enforces at the right moments.

## 5. Headless / statusline / SDK

`claude -p` headless mode: JSON/stream-JSON output, `--continue`/`--resume`, auto-approve flags — our cheap summarizer can itself be a headless Claude (or any small model) run out-of-band. Claude Code can run *as* an MCP server (`claude mcp serve`). Statusline: any script, receives rich JSON (session_id, transcript_path, model, context %, cost, worktree/PR info) on stdin every update — perfect low-friction **teammate-presence display** ("Can is in match.service.ts"). Also useful: `FileChanged` hook and `CLAUDE_ENV`-style session env; SDK (Agent SDK) exposes the same hooks programmatically.

## Feasibility A–E

**A. Transcript-tailing daemon + summarizer.** Effort **M** (watcher is easy; robust JSONL parsing across versions, subagent dirs, redaction and LLM cost make it M). Reliability: high capture fidelity, zero agent-behavior risk, works even if hooks are misconfigured; schema is undocumented/unstable (version field helps). Privacy: **highest risk** — raw everything; must summarize locally + human-gate uploads.

**B. Stop/PostToolUse-hook summarization.** Effort **S** — Stop hook gets `transcript_path` + `last_assistant_message`; `async:true` avoids blocking. Reliability high (deterministic firing; SubagentStop covers subagents). Privacy: same data, but event-scoped chunks are easier to redact. Strictly dominates A for MVP; A only wins for crash/abandon capture.

**C. SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit injection.** Effort **S/M** (S for the hook; M for the retrieval backend). Reliability high — `additionalContext` is guaranteed delivery; UserPromptSubmit gives per-prompt semantic matching. Latency budget matters (hook blocks prompt; keep <1s or go async). Privacy: low (inbound only, but prompts are sent to the service for matching — hash/em­bed locally if needed).

**D. MCP server (publish_diagnosis, search_related_work, extend_diagnosis, ask_agent).** Effort **M**. Reliability of *invocation* is the weak point — mitigate with C's reminders and skill triggers. Privacy: **best** — agent-mediated, explicit, human-visible tool calls; natural approval gate. This is where the diagnosis graph lives.

**E. PreToolUse conflict tripwire on Edit/Write.** Effort **S** (given presence data from B/C). Reliability: excellent mechanism (`ask` + reason is ideal — warns without hard-blocking); needs fast (<300ms, cached) presence lookup. Privacy: minimal (file paths only).

**Ship first: B + C + D, then E; skip A initially.** B gives passive capture cheaply via supported APIs; C closes the loop with guaranteed injection of teammates' findings; D is the structured knowledge core the other two feed and the only way agents *extend* diagnoses. E is a near-free add-on once presence exists. All four distribute via one committed `.claude/settings.json` + `.mcp.json` in the team repo — installation is a single PR. Channels-based push and transcript tailing are v2 candidates once the schema/preview stabilize.

# Storage, Search, and Realtime Recommendation

## 1. Store: Postgres 17 + pgvector, single store. No Redis, no SQLite mode.

**Recommendation:** One `docker-compose.yml` with two services: the app and `pgvector/pgvector:pg17`. That meets "self-hostable in <10 minutes" and scales far past 50 devs.

- **Skip SQLite+sqlite-vec dev mode.** It would mean two query dialects, two FTS implementations, and two vector code paths forever — permanent tax for a marginal install win (Docker compose *is* the zero-dep mode in practice). sqlite-vec is legitimate for embedded/local-first, but this service is inherently multi-writer/multi-reader, which is Postgres's home turf.
- **Skip Redis.** At 50 devs (~100–200 concurrent agent sessions, event rates of a few/second at worst), Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY` easily covers realtime wake-ups. Its real limits — 8 KB payload cap, ephemeral delivery (missed if disconnected), commit-time global-queue contention at high txn rates — don't bite here, *provided you use it correctly*: **outbox pattern**. Write every event as a row in `events`, then `NOTIFY events_channel` with only the event id. Connectors that reconnect replay from their cursor; NOTIFY is purely a latency optimization over polling. This gives you durability that Redis pub/sub doesn't even have.
- **ORM/migrations (TypeScript service):** **Drizzle + drizzle-kit.** Native `vector()` column type and `cosineDistance` operator, first-class `tsvector`/JSONB/array support, plain-SQL escape hatch you'll need for the RRF query and recursive CTEs over the claim graph. Prisma still treats `vector` as `Unsupported()` in schema and forces `$queryRaw` for every vector op. Runtime: Node/Bun + Hono or Fastify — one service, one language. **Don't add a Python service**; if a Python connector-SDK exists later it's just an HTTP client. (If you ever did need Python server-side: SQLAlchemy + Alembic + `pgvector-python`, but keep migrations owned by drizzle-kit only — one migration authority.)

## 2. Search: hybrid (FTS + vector, RRF) over a *structured normalization* — not vector-only

**Hybrid, from day one.** Bug investigations are full of exact tokens embeddings blur (`match.service.ts`, `NullPointerException`, `column_preset`, error codes) and paraphrases FTS misses ("starts column reads zero" vs "appearances aggregate wrong"). Published measurements consistently show large precision gains from fusing FTS with vectors via RRF (~62%→84% in one RAG benchmark). Implementation is one SQL CTE: `tsvector`/`websearch_to_tsquery` ranked list + pgvector cosine ranked list, fused with `1/(60+rank)`. Native `ts_rank_cd` is not true BM25 but is fine at this corpus size; ParadeDB `pg_search` is a later upgrade, not v0.

**What semantic matching of two differently-worded investigations actually requires:** plain embeddings over raw session text underperform badly — most of the text is boilerplate (paths, commands, agent chatter) and the cosine neighborhood collapses. You need **embeddings over a normalized "search document" plus exact matching on extracted entities**:

- The connector (or a cheap LLM pass) extracts per work-context: **components touched, file paths, symbols, symptom phrases ("X shows zero when Y"), error fingerprints** (stack traces with line numbers/addresses/UUIDs stripped, then hashed).
- Exact/overlap matching on files, symbols, and error fingerprints is the highest-precision collision signal — deterministic, no embeddings needed.
- Embeddings are computed over the normalized doc (`title + symptom phrases + component names + hypothesis summaries`), catching "different vocabulary, same bug." Claims get their own embeddings for diagnosis-level matching.

**Embedding models — pluggable provider interface, two blessed defaults:**
- **Hosted default: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`** (1536-d, ~$0.02/1M tokens — effectively free at this volume; use the `dimensions` param to truncate to 768 so both defaults share one column width). Voyage is better on code but adds a niche key requirement; not the default.
- **Local default: Ollama `nomic-embed-text`** (768-d, light, good enough). `bge-m3` (1024-d) if the team is multilingual — but then dims differ, so:
- Store `embedding_model` in a config row; **changing model = re-embed migration** (corpus is tiny, minutes). Don't build multi-model columns.

## 3. Data model (SQL-ish sketch)

```sql
-- v0 -----------------------------------------------------------------
teams(id pk, name, created_at)                      -- single row in v0
developers(id pk, team_id fk, name, email unique,
           api_key_hash, role text default 'member', created_at)

agent_sessions(id pk, developer_id fk, agent_kind,   -- 'claude-code'|...
    repo, branch, base_commit,
    status,   -- analyzing|planning|implementing|testing|blocked|done
    started_at, last_heartbeat_at, ended_at)
-- presence = last_heartbeat_at > now()-interval '90s'; TTL by query, no deletes

work_contexts(id pk, session_id fk, repo, branch, base_commit,
    title, description, intent jsonb,     -- planned changes/APIs/side-effects
    status, normalized_doc text,          -- the embedding/FTS source
    tsv tsvector generated always as (to_tsvector('english', normalized_doc)) stored,
    embedding vector(768), created_at, updated_at)

work_context_targets(work_context_id fk,             -- exact-overlap signals
    kind,   -- file|symbol|component|api|error_fingerprint
    value text, primary key(work_context_id, kind, value))

claims(id pk, work_context_id fk, author_session_id fk,
    kind,       -- observation|hypothesis|evidence|root_cause|decision|rejected_approach
    body text, confidence real,           -- 0..1
    status,     -- proposed|partially_confirmed|likely_root_cause|rejected|superseded
    tsv tsvector, embedding vector(768), created_at)
-- append-only: revisions supersede via edge, never UPDATE body

claim_edges(id pk, from_claim fk, to_claim fk,
    kind,       -- supports|contradicts|deeper_cause_of|supersedes|relates_to
    author_session_id fk, note text, created_at,
    unique(from_claim, to_claim, kind))
-- "your root cause is my symptom" = new claim + deeper_cause_of edge; recursive CTE walks chains

artifacts(id pk, claim_id fk, kind,       -- log|stack_trace|diff_summary|command_output
    content text, sensitivity,            -- team_visible|needs_approval
    approved_by fk null, approved_at, created_at)
-- needs_approval content returned only to owner until approved (full diffs live here)

events(id bigserial pk, team_id fk, kind, payload jsonb, created_at)
-- outbox: overlap_warning|claim_added|session_started|...; NOTIFY on insert; SSE replays by id cursor

-- LATER --------------------------------------------------------------
-- subscriptions(developer_id, filter jsonb)  -- v0: everyone gets team events
-- questions(from_session, to_session, body, answer)  -- agent-to-agent Q&A
-- multi-team tenancy enforcement, per-repo ACLs, claim revision history table
```

## 4. Realtime + auth

- **SSE, not WebSocket.** Connector→server traffic is ordinary request/response HTTP (register session, heartbeat, post claims, query); only server→connector needs push. SSE gives auto-reconnect with `Last-Event-Id` mapping directly onto the `events` cursor, works through proxies, plain HTTP auth headers, ~150 idle connections is nothing for Node. Polling `GET /events?after=<id>` is the automatic degraded mode — same endpoint semantics.
- **Auth: per-dev API keys, not a shared team token.** Provenance is a core feature (who claimed what); a shared token destroys attribution and revocability (one laptop stolen = rotate everyone). Bootstrap: `ADMIN_TOKEN` env var → admin creates developers → each gets a bearer key (store SHA-256 hash). TLS via the user's reverse proxy or Tailscale; document both, build neither.

## 5. Do NOT build in v0

- Redis, message queues, or any second datastore; WebSockets; a graph database (edges-as-rows + recursive CTE suffices)
- ParadeDB/BM25 extension, cross-encoder rerankers, multi-model embedding storage
- Multi-team tenancy enforcement, per-repo ACLs, OAuth/SSO
- Agent-to-agent chat/questions, subscription filters (v0: team-wide fan-out)
- Approval *workflow UI* (v0: sensitivity flag + one approve endpoint)
- Kubernetes/Helm charts; a Python server; connector SDKs beyond Claude Code hooks + plain HTTP

Sources: [PgDog on LISTEN/NOTIFY scaling](https://pgdog.dev/blog/scaling-postgres-listen-notify), [Prisma blog: Postgres pub/sub](https://www.prisma.io/blog/you-dont-need-redis-postgres-already-has-pub-sub), [Stacksync: 8KB limit and beyond](https://www.stacksync.com/blog/beyond-listen-notify-postgres-request-reply-real-time-sync), [Jonathan Katz: hybrid search in Postgres](https://jkatz05.com/post/postgres/hybrid-search-postgres-pgvector/), [ParadeDB hybrid search manual](https://www.paradedb.com/blog/hybrid-search-in-postgresql-the-missing-manual), [RRF hybrid search precision numbers](https://dev.to/gabrielanhaia/hybrid-search-in-100-lines-bm25-pgvector-with-rrf-merge-58cn), [Drizzle vs Prisma 2026](https://encore.dev/articles/drizzle-vs-prisma), [sqlite-vec vs pgvector](https://grokipedia.com/page/Comparison_of_sqlite-vec_and_pgvector)

# Architect A Proposal — Adoption-First / Local-First

Working name: **groundcrew** (CLI: `crew`). North star: a 2-dev team gets visible value in <10 minutes, with zero change to how anyone works.

## 1. Architecture overview

**Backend choice — alternatives considered honestly.** (a) *Git-backed* (beads/Entire pattern): zero infra, reuses trusted auth — but sync latency reintroduces exactly the "git is too late" failure, and per-prompt injection needs sub-second reads. Rejected as primary; kept as an export format. (b) *Serverless free tier* (Overlap's Cloudflare story): nice deploy tale, but vendor coupling, cold starts on the prompt-blocking path, and no offline degrade. Rejected. (c) *P2P/CRDT*: NAT pain, no durable team memory. Rejected. **Chosen: one self-hosted process, embedded database.** `npx groundcrew serve` runs a Bun/Hono service with **PGlite + pgvector** (Postgres-in-WASM) embedded — no Docker, no DB install. `DATABASE_URL` flips the same Drizzle code to real Postgres for big teams. This *partially disagrees with the storage digest's "no SQLite mode"*: its real objection was two dialects forever; PGlite keeps **one dialect** (Postgres, tsvector, pgvector) with two runtimes, so the tax it feared doesn't exist. Host on any teammate's laptop + Tailscale, or a $5 VPS. I also drop the sketch's FastAPI/Redis/WebSockets entirely (per digest: SSE + outbox + one language).

**No daemon.** The connector is hooks + an MCP server only — short-lived processes, nothing to babysit. Offline spool is flushed opportunistically by the next hook invocation. (The ACP proxy daemon is the v1 agent-agnostic path.)

```
Dev A machine                                Dev B machine
┌───────────────────────────┐               ┌─────────────────────┐
│ Claude Code               │               │ Claude Code         │
│ ├ hooks: capture+inject   │               │ ├ hooks             │
│ ├ MCP tools (diagnosis)   │               │ ├ MCP tools         │
│ ├ statusline: presence    │               │ └ statusline        │
│ ├ spool ~/.crew/ (offline)│               │                     │
│ └ Stop→ claude -p (haiku) │               │                     │
└──────────┬────────────────┘               └─────────┬───────────┘
      HTTPS + SSE (Last-Event-Id cursor)         HTTPS + SSE
           └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                 ┌─────────▼──────────────────────┐
                 │ `crew serve` — single process  │
                 │ Hono API · SSE · outbox events │
                 │ PGlite+pgvector | Postgres     │
                 │ presence · claims · hybrid RRF │
                 └────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Install** = one PR: `crew init` writes `.claude/settings.json` (hooks, statusline) + `.mcp.json` (project scope) into the repo. Every teammate is connected on next `git pull`. `crew login <url>` stores a per-dev API key once.

## 2. Capture pipeline (knowledge OUT)

Per the integration digest: ship **B + C + D**, skip transcript-tailing (A).

- **SessionStart hook**: registers session — `repo, branch, base_commit` (from git), dev, agent, cwd. Fails open in 400ms.
- **PostToolUse (`async: true`) on Edit/Write/Bash**: appends *targets* (file paths; symbols via a cheap tree-sitter pass; error fingerprints from failed command output — stack traces with line numbers/UUIDs stripped, hashed). Doubles as heartbeat. Zero tokens, zero latency.
- **Stop hook (`async: true`) → summarizer**: triggers on turn end; spawns `claude -p --model haiku` over the turn delta (`transcript_path` tail + `last_assistant_message`). **No new API key** — reuses the dev's existing Claude Code auth. It emits one structured record, zod-validated (reject on schema failure), secret-scanned (gitleaks-style regexes) **locally before upload**:

```json
{ "status": "analyzing", "title": "Starts column zero on evergreen cubes",
  "symptoms": ["appearance aggregate reads 0 when lineup dropped"],
  "targets": {"files": ["match.service.ts"], "error_fingerprints": ["a1b2…"]},
  "claims": [{"kind": "hypothesis", "body": "cube v2 denominator drops presence rows",
              "status": "proposed", "confidence": 0.5, "evidence_refs": []}],
  "rejected": [{"body": "entity-resolution mismatch", "reason": "IDs verified equal"}] }
```

- **MCP tools (the quality path)**: `publish_diagnosis`, `extend_diagnosis` (add claims/edges to *someone else's* tree — e.g. `deeper_cause_of`), `search_related_work`, `get_team_context`, `request_share` (artifacts). MCP invocation is unreliable (integration digest §4), so hook-injected reminders nudge at the right moments ("a related open diagnosis by Can exists; extend it via `extend_diagnosis`"). Passive Stop-hook capture is the floor; agent-authored claims are the ceiling.
- **SessionEnd**: closes session; unsynced records stay spooled and flush on next session.

Full diffs, logs, transcripts never auto-upload: artifacts default `needs_approval`; `crew approve <id>` (v0) releases them.

## 3. Injection/delivery (knowledge IN)

All delivery is hook-driven `additionalContext` (guaranteed, per digest; MCP channels push is preview-gated — v1).

- **SessionStart briefing** (≤600 tokens): active teammates in this repo, overlapping targets, open diagnoses touching the same components, recent merged outcomes.
- **UserPromptSubmit** (≤300 tokens, 400ms timeout, fail-open): the prompt is matched via **hybrid FTS + pgvector RRF** over normalized docs, plus exact overlap on files/symbols/error fingerprints (highest-precision signal, no embeddings needed). Inject **max 3 hits above threshold**. Embeddings are an *optional enhancer*: with no key configured, matching degrades to FTS + exact targets and still works — no mandatory OpenAI dependency (adoption-first disagreement with the digest's hosted default). Configured: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` @768d or Ollama `nomic-embed-text`.
- **Anti-anchoring format** — every hint carries provenance, status, evidence count, age, phrased as factual statements (prompt-injection defenses, per docs): *"Can's session (2h ago) holds hypothesis H (status: proposed, unverified, 0 evidence items) for symptom S. It has NOT been confirmed. Can's session rejected approach R because …"* Rules: `rejected_approach` and `likely_root_cause` inject prominently (high value, low anchoring risk); bare `proposed` hypotheses inject only with an explicit unverified marker; a claim id is never re-injected in the same session (connector seen-set).
- **Statusline** = human-facing presence ("Can → match.service.ts · debugging starts column"), polled with a short cache. Zero tokens, and it's the first-run wow: two terminals, each sees the other within seconds of install.
- **v0.5 — PreToolUse tripwire** on Edit/Write: cached presence lookup (<300ms); tempo's escalation ladder — clear → `additionalContext` notice → `permissionDecision: "ask"` with reason on hard overlap (same file+symbol, active teammate). Never hard-deny.

## 4. Core data model

Adopting the storage digest's schema nearly verbatim (it's right):

- **developers**(id, name, email, api_key_hash)
- **agent_sessions**(id, developer_id, agent_kind, repo, branch, base_commit, status, last_heartbeat_at) — presence = heartbeat < 90s, TTL by query
- **work_contexts**(id, session_id, title, intent jsonb, status, normalized_doc, tsv generated, embedding vector(768) nullable)
- **work_context_targets**(work_context_id, kind: file|symbol|component|error_fingerprint, value)
- **claims**(id, work_context_id, author_session_id, kind: observation|hypothesis|evidence|root_cause|decision|rejected_approach, body, confidence, status: proposed|partially_confirmed|likely_root_cause|rejected|superseded, tsv, embedding) — append-only
- **claim_edges**(from, to, kind: supports|contradicts|deeper_cause_of|supersedes|relates_to, author, note) — omem's reconcile verbs; recursive CTE walks chains
- **artifacts**(claim_id, kind, content, sensitivity: team_visible|needs_approval, approved_by)
- **events**(bigserial, kind, payload) — outbox; in-process emitter (PGlite) or NOTIFY (Postgres) wakes SSE; cursor replay via `Last-Event-Id`

## 5. Repo layout (TypeScript-only monorepo, Bun)

```
apps/server/          Hono API + SSE + hybrid search (PGlite|Postgres)
apps/web/             read-only feed + approvals UI (v0.5, Vite/React)
packages/db/          drizzle schema + migrations (single authority)
packages/schema/      zod record/claim/event types = the wire protocol
packages/connector-claude/  hook scripts, MCP server, statusline, spool
packages/cli/         crew: serve|init|login|status|approve|mute|export
docs/  examples/
```

## 6. MVP cut

**v0 (2 weeks, ruthless):** `crew serve` (embedded PGlite) · `crew init/login` · session registration + heartbeat presence · statusline display · Stop-hook summarizer → work_contexts/targets/claims · SessionStart briefing · UserPromptSubmit injection (FTS + exact-target; vectors if key present) · MCP `publish/extend/search` · exact-overlap warnings (files/symbols/fingerprints only — deterministic) · spool + fail-open everywhere · `crew approve` CLI. **No** web UI, no PreToolUse gating, no edges UI, no Cursor.
**v0.5:** PreToolUse tripwire (ask-mode) · web feed + approval UI · `contradicts` surfacing ("two open root-cause theories for one fingerprint") · injection telemetry (were hints used?) · git-bundle export.
**v1:** ACP proxy connector (agent-agnostic: one connector for all ACP agents) · semantic/architectural conflict detector · agent-to-agent questions (A2A-extension-shaped payloads) · MCP channels push · OTel GenAI event export · Postgres scale-out + auth hardening docs.

## 7. Non-goals for v1

- **Git-as-primary-transport** — kills liveness, the core wedge (export only).
- **Redis, WebSockets, graph DB, queues** — SSE + outbox + edge rows suffice at 50 devs (digest).
- **Transcript-tailing daemon** — Stop hook dominates for MVP; raw-transcript privacy risk not worth crash-capture.
- **Multi-team tenancy, SSO/OAuth, per-repo ACLs** — TLS via reverse proxy/Tailscale, documented not built.
- **Yet-another-team-memory MCP as headline** — that lane is commoditized (prior art); the diagnosis graph + injection is the product.
- **Agent chat, rerankers, ParadeDB, VS Code extension, hosted SaaS.**

## 8. Top 5 risks

1. **Noisy/false-positive hints** (worst failure: devs uninstall). Hard budgets (≤3 hits, ≤300 tokens), score threshold auto-raised when telemetry shows injected claims go unused, seen-set dedup, `crew mute`, ask-never-deny gating.
2. **Privacy leak.** Local-only summarization, schema-constrained output, secret-scan before upload, artifacts default `needs_approval` with elicitation/CLI consent, per-dev keys (attribution + revocation), fully self-hosted.
3. **Capture quality** (garbage claims poison the graph). Zod validation with reject, confidence + provenance always displayed so agents discount, MCP explicit publishing as the trusted tier, golden-transcript eval fixtures in CI.
4. **Adoption friction.** One `npx` to serve, one PR to onboard the whole team, no Docker, no new API keys, zero behavior change, fail-open when the service is down, and solo-dev value on day one (your own cross-session memory + statusline) so a 1-person trial sticks before the team joins.
5. **Staleness/anchoring on dead work.** Heartbeat-TTL presence, age-decayed match scores, `supersedes` edges, merged-branch detection (base_commit reachable from main ⇒ context marked *landed*), and every injected hint timestamped with status so the agent treats old hypotheses as history, not truth.

# Architecture Proposal — "AWP": an open Agent Work-State Protocol + reference hub

**Thesis (Architect B):** The durable artifact is not a server — it is an open, versioned schema for *in-flight work state and diagnosis exchange*, the way LSP outlived every editor. Every competitor in the prior-art digest died as a product (Overlap, asynkor, tempo, ai-team-sync all <100 stars, stalled in months) because each welded its data model to one delivery mechanism. We ship a spec + conformance fixtures + a reference hub + a Claude Code adapter. Cursor/Codex/ACP adapters become mappings, not rewrites.

**Explicit disagreements with the original sketch:** (1) No Redis, no WebSockets — Postgres outbox + `NOTIFY` + SSE with `Last-Event-Id` cursors covers 50 devs with durability Redis pub/sub lacks. (2) No FastAPI option — one language (TypeScript), one migration authority (drizzle-kit). (3) No standing local "agent-connector daemon" — Claude Code hooks call the hub directly (HTTP hooks exist); a daemon is v2 if crash-capture matters. (4) "Semantic matching" is demoted: deterministic entity overlap (files, symbols, error fingerprints) is the primary signal; embeddings are the recall booster, not the foundation. (5) Automatic "diagnostic/architectural conflict detection" is cut from v1 — contradictions are *explicit claim edges* agents assert; inferring them is a research project. (6) Agent-to-agent questions are cut — the digest shows A2A-style peer messaging is the wrong topology; keep payloads A2A-extension-shaped for later.

## 1. Architecture overview

Hub-and-spoke. Adapters translate agent-native surfaces into AWP records (capture) and AWP hints into agent-native injection (delivery). The hub is a reference implementation of the transport contract; the spec also defines a non-normative git-JSONL transport (beads/Entire pattern) for server-averse teams.

```
 Dev A machine                          Team hub (reference impl)          Dev B machine
┌─────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐
│ Claude Code             │        │ Bun/Node + Hono              │   │ Claude Code     │
│  ├ hooks ──────────────────HTTP──▶ /sessions /claims /match     │   │  ◀ hooks ◀──┐   │
│  │  SessionStart/Prompt │        │ Postgres17 + pgvector        │   │             │   │
│  │  PostToolUse/Stop    │        │  sessions │ claims+edges     │   │  MCP tools  │   │
│  ├ MCP server (stdio)───────HTTP──▶  targets │ events(outbox)   │───SSE──────────┘   │
│  │  awp_publish/search  │        │ hybrid search (FTS+vec, RRF) │   └─────────────────┘
│  └ local summarizer     │        │ per-dev API keys, approvals  │
│    (headless claude -p) │        └──────────────────────────────┘
└─────────────────────────┘        spec/ = JSON Schemas + fixtures (the actual product)
```

**Protocol contract (v0.1):** Every record is self-contained JSON: `{awp:"0.1", id:ULID, ts, producer:{developer, agent_kind, session_id}, kind, body}`. Additive changes = minor version; consumers MUST ignore unknown fields and kinds (forward compat). Two record families: **work-state events** (session lifecycle, heartbeat, targets, intent) and **claims** (diagnosis graph). Observation events carry OTel `gen_ai.*` attributes (pinned semconv) so the stream exports to any OTel backend free.

## 2. Capture pipeline (out of a live session)

Ship path B + C + D + E from the integration digest; skip transcript tailing (A).

- **SessionStart hook** → `POST /sessions`: repo, branch, `base_commit` (from `git rev-parse`), cwd, developer key, agent_kind. Response doubles as briefing (see §3).
- **PostToolUse hook** (Edit/Write/Bash matchers, `async:true`) → heartbeat + target upsert: file paths from `tool_input`, error fingerprints from failed Bash output (stack trace with line numbers/UUIDs stripped, hashed). No LLM, <50ms, fire-and-forget.
- **Stop hook** (`async:true`) → triggers the **local summarizer**: headless `claude -p` (Haiku-class) over the last turn's transcript slice, emitting schema-validated claim candidates. Runs on the dev's machine — raw transcript never leaves it. Output posted as claims with `provenance:"derived"` and confidence capped at 0.5.
- **MCP tools** (the only path for *authoritative* knowledge): `awp_briefing`, `awp_search`, `awp_publish_claim`, `awp_extend` (add edge to someone else's claim), `awp_share_artifact` (sensitivity-gated). Claims published here get `provenance:"declared"`. Invocation reliability is MCP's weak point, so injected system reminders (UserPromptSubmit) nudge: "unpublished hypothesis detected — consider awp_publish_claim." Never PreToolUse-deny to force it in v0.

**Structured claim record:**

```json
{"awp":"0.1","kind":"claim","body":{
  "work_context":"wc_01J...","claim_kind":"hypothesis",
  "text":"Starts column zero because cube v2 denominator drops tactics-lineup rows",
  "status":"partially_confirmed","confidence":0.6,"provenance":"declared",
  "entities":{"files":["match.service.ts"],"symbols":["buildAppearanceAgg"],
              "error_fp":["sha256:ab12..."]},
  "evidence_refs":["cl_01H..."]}}
```

## 3. Injection/delivery (into a session)

Three moments, strict budgets, escalation-ladder semantics (tempo's clear/notice/stop, reborn as inject/hint/ask):

- **SessionStart** (`additionalContext`): the briefing. Max ~1,200 tokens: teammates active on this repo (presence = heartbeat <90s), top-3 related work contexts (hybrid match on repo+branch+recent commits), open contradictions touching this area. Re-fires on resume.
- **UserPromptSubmit** (sync, 800ms budget): hub runs the fast path only (entity overlap + FTS); vector results, if late, arrive next turn via an async hook. Max **one** hint ≤300 tokens, only above a precision threshold. Anything weaker is silently dropped — a wrong hint costs more than a missed one.
- **PreToolUse on Edit/Write** (tripwire): target file overlaps an *active* teammate session → `permissionDecision:"ask"` with reason ("Can's session is editing match.service.ts, status: implementing, 12m ago"). Never `deny` in v0. Cached presence lookup, <300ms.

**Anti-anchoring is a protocol requirement, not a UX nicety.** Every hint the hub emits MUST carry: author, age, hypothesis `status`, `confidence`, `provenance` (declared vs derived), and **commit drift** ("based on a commit 14 behind your HEAD"). Adapters MUST render hints as factual provenance-first statements — "Can's session (2h ago) holds hypothesis X at status partially_confirmed, confidence 0.6; unverified" — never as instructions (this also matches Claude Code's prompt-injection guidance). The highest-value, lowest-anchoring payload is prioritized first: **rejected hypotheses with evidence** ("already ruled out: caching theory, see evidence cl_...") — negative knowledge cannot anchor you on a wrong answer, only save you a dead end. Ranking decays by age and drift; sessions past heartbeat TTL are excluded from tripwires and demoted in briefings.

## 4. Core data model

Adopting the storage digest's sketch nearly verbatim (Postgres 17 + pgvector, Drizzle):

- **developers** (id, name, email, api_key_hash) — per-dev keys; provenance is a feature.
- **agent_sessions** (developer, agent_kind, repo, branch, base_commit, status: analyzing…done, last_heartbeat_at) — presence by TTL query, no deletes.
- **work_contexts** (session, title, intent jsonb, normalized_doc, tsv generated, embedding vector(768)) — the embedding source is the *normalized* doc (title + symptoms + components + hypothesis summaries), never raw transcript.
- **work_context_targets** (kind: file|symbol|component|api|error_fingerprint, value) — the deterministic overlap index.
- **claims** (work_context, author_session, kind: observation|hypothesis|evidence|root_cause|decision|rejected_approach, body, confidence, status, provenance, tsv, embedding) — **append-only**; revision = new claim + supersedes edge.
- **claim_edges** (from, to, kind: supports|contradicts|deeper_cause_of|supersedes|relates_to, author, note) — omem's reconciliation verbs; "your root cause is my symptom" = new claim + `deeper_cause_of`. Recursive CTE walks chains; no graph DB.
- **artifacts** (claim, kind: log|stack_trace|diff_summary, content, sensitivity: team_visible|needs_approval, approved_by) — full diffs live here, owner-only until approved.
- **events** (bigserial, kind, payload) — outbox; `NOTIFY` on insert; SSE replays from cursor.

## 5. Repo layout

```
awp/                       # TypeScript monorepo (Bun workspaces)
  spec/                    # JSON Schemas, protocol doc, versioning policy,
                           #   conformance fixtures  ← the product
  packages/types/          # zod schemas + TS types generated from spec
  packages/hub/            # reference server: Hono, Drizzle, pg17+pgvector
  packages/adapter-claude/ # hook scripts, MCP server (stdio), summarizer prompt,
                           #   installer (npx awp init → writes .claude/settings.json + .mcp.json)
  packages/cli/            # awp status / approve / key management
  packages/conformance/    # transport + adapter test harness against fixtures
  apps/dashboard/          # v0.5: read-only web UI
  docker-compose.yml       # app + pgvector/pgvector:pg17 — the <10-min install
```

Python appears only ever as a generated HTTP client. Embeddings pluggable: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` truncated to 768d (hosted default) or Ollama `nomic-embed-text` (local default); model change = re-embed migration.

## 6. MVP cut

**v0 (2 weeks):**
- Week 1: spec v0.1 frozen (envelope, session/claim/edge/hint schemas, transport contract, fixtures); hub: auth, sessions/heartbeat/targets, claims+edges, hybrid search (one RRF CTE), events+SSE.
- Week 2: Claude adapter: SessionStart briefing, PostToolUse targets, Stop summarizer, 5 MCP tools, UserPromptSubmit hint, PreToolUse tripwire; `npx awp init`; docker-compose. Installation for a whole team = one committed PR.
- This covers all five original MVP functions. Cut from v0: dashboard, artifacts/approvals, subscriptions.

**v0.5:** artifacts + approval gate (flag + one approve endpoint/CLI; MCP elicitation UI when convenient), read-only dashboard, contradiction surfacing in briefings, dismissal telemetry to tune thresholds.

**v1:** **ACP proxy adapter** — one connector between editor and any ACP agent (JetBrains, Zed, Gemini CLI, 25+ registered) mirrors normalized session events to the hub; this is the agent-agnostic bet paying off. Plus git-JSONL transport, Cursor rules adapter, per-dev subscription filters, OTel exporter.

## 7. Non-goals for v1

- **General "team memory."** The 0–30-star team-memory-MCP graveyard proves the lane is commoditized. We store in-flight work state only.
- **Automatic semantic/architectural conflict inference.** Tempo's abandoned prototype is the cautionary tale; explicit `contradicts` edges + overlap tripwires deliver 80% of the value deterministically.
- **Agent-to-agent messaging / A2A.** Wrong topology (hub-and-spoke, not peer services); payloads stay A2A-extension-shaped for a future SEP.
- **Redis, queues, WebSockets, graph DB, ParadeDB, rerankers, SSO, multi-tenancy** — per storage digest; every one is a second system to operate.
- **Transcript-tailing daemon.** Stop-hook capture dominates for MVP; the JSONL schema is undocumented and privacy-hot.
- **Approval workflow UI.** Flag + endpoint suffices until someone asks.

## 8. Top 5 risks

1. **Noise / false-positive hints** (worst failure: anchoring a healthy agent on a teammate's wrong theory). Mitigate: precision-first thresholds (vector-only matches never trigger interrupts, only briefing entries), 1 hint/prompt and 3/session budget, rejected-hypotheses-first ordering, mandatory status/confidence/drift on every hint, per-dev mute, dismissal metrics from day one.
2. **Privacy.** Raw transcripts and diffs never leave the machine: summarization and entity extraction run locally; only normalized docs, entities, and claims upload; secret-pattern scrub before POST; artifacts default `needs_approval`; per-dev revocable keys.
3. **Capture quality** (derived claims are garbage). Mitigate: provenance flag with confidence cap 0.5 for derived claims, schema validation + linting at ingest, injected nudges toward explicit `awp_publish_claim`, conformance fixtures so every adapter's output is testable.
4. **Adoption friction.** One-PR team install; compose-up hub in <10 minutes; solo-useful on day one (briefings = your own session continuity) so value doesn't wait on network effects; zero-workflow-change passive capture (Overlap's lesson); "GitHub sees the past, we see the present" positioning.
5. **Staleness.** Heartbeat TTL kills ghost presence; commit-drift computed against the reader's HEAD and shown in every hint; age decay in ranking; `supersedes`/`contradicts` edges demote stale root causes; `likely_root_cause` status requires ≥1 evidence link; SessionEnd closes contexts automatically.
